redFirst.basis: regression task, expectRedFirst false; the failure only reproduces on windows-latest, which cannot be run here

outcome.technical: Product file is not at fault: plugins/audit/hooks/py-launch.sh has 0 CR bytes (grep -c $'\r' = 0), .gitattributes pins '* text=auto eol=lf' and '*.sh text eol=lf', and 'bash --posix -n' (homebrew 5.3 and /bin/bash) and 'dash -n' all exit 0 on it. hooks.json runs it as sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/py-launch.sh" ..., i.e. from a file on disk, never as -c text. The failing path is the test's _drive_as(), which passed the whole 113-line launcher body as the sh -c argv element; on Windows that multi-line text with quotes/backslashes crosses Python's MSVCRT quoting and the MSYS runtime's own re-split, and reached Git's sh as text with an unterminated case (REASONED from the CI error 'line 114: unexpected end of file from case on line 65'; not run on Windows). Fix (test only): _drive_as now runs sh -c '. "$3"' <dollar0> <script> <mode> <launcher path> so the launcher is sourced from disk and sees $0/$1/$2 as under test; $0 stays exactly the backslash/mixed spelling. Local: test_py_launch.py --selftest 22/22 pass (pl20-pl22 included); sweep-selftests full run started in background, not awaited. Assumptions about Windows: (1) Git's sh passes $0 of a -c command through verbatim (CI output shows the $0 values echoed intact, e.g. 'hooks\\.\\py-launch.sh: -c'); (2) the '.' builtin sources a forward-slash drive path (C:/...) in MSYS sh, and a sourced file sees the -c positionals (POSIX). Neither verified on Windows; the orchestrator's next CI run settles it. py-launch.sh unchanged, still POSIX builtins only.
outcome.descriptive: Windows pl20-pl22 failure traced to the test handing the launcher text to sh -c; the test now sources the launcher from disk, the shipped hook is unchanged.
